input: With regard to the staffing ramp, it is proposed that the figure be held at 12%, notwithstanding the suggestion that a lower figure might be adopted. The concern with a lower alternative is that the work fronts on the upgrade project would not be covered as the planned sequence reaches its busiest period, and the saving in the early period would be bought at the price of uncovered work later on. The underlying figures are set out in the Costs section, and they are not repeated here; the present point is concerned only with the level of the ramp itself. It is accordingly suggested that the steering group retain the figure as proposed, since the ramp has been set against the sequence of work it has to serve, and a reduction at this stage would reopen a balance that has already been struck between coverage and cost. To reduce the ramp at this stage would therefore be to revisit that balance in the absence of any change in the underlying sequence of work, and it is difficult to see what would have changed in order to justify such a revisit.
target: The staffing ramp for the upgrade project is held at 12%. A lower alternative leaves work fronts uncovered as the planned sequence reaches its busiest period, and the early saving is bought with uncovered work later. The ramp is set against the sequence of work it has to serve, and the figure is defended on coverage, not on cost: the cost table stands in the Costs section, and its figures are not repeated here. The steering group is asked to retain the figure. The defence is about timing as much as about totals: a ramp set below the sequence it serves does not distribute the same staff more thinly, it leaves particular fronts unstaffed at the point where the sequence needs them, and late cover costs more than early cover because the work has by then been waiting. The figure is therefore the lowest figure consistent with the sequence, not a figure with slack left in it. Holding the ramp also holds the recruitment and clearance lead times that the sequence assumes. A reduction at this stage reopens the balance already struck between coverage and cost, and the balance was struck with the full sequence in view.
